title: Blit - The Code First, AI Native Pixel Editor, free and open source
author: 314t
selftext:
You guys asked for it, so I am making the code open source. Create pixel art in code.

[https://github.com/choobi-doobi/blit-standalone](https://github.com/choobi-doobi/blit-standalone)

**Supports**

* Live coding. Type and the canvas updates as it plays, with no restart. If a run breaks, the last good frame stays on screen.
* Click-to-paint. Click a pixel and it edits the character in the code that drew it, even through mirrors, offsets and rotations.
* Sprites as text. Hand-drawn sprite literals, palettes and ramps, outlines, dithering, tiling rules. They all compose like Strudel patterns.
* Animation. Frames, cycles and time operators, plus onion skinning. Edit a walk cycle while it's walking.
* Scenes. Place saved sketches on a canvas and drag them around.
* Audio reactive. Turn on the mic and sketches react to the beat and frequency bands.
* Export. PNG frames, spritesheets, looping GIFs, Aseprite files, or the source itself.
* Import. Drop in a PNG and it becomes an editable sprite.
* AI native. It ships with an MCP server, so Claude or any other MCP agent can create, edit, lint and delete sketches. It can also render a PNG to check its own work. Most of the iso pieces in the video were built this way.
* **MIT Licensed**
